title: Multiphase conjecture
formal: Do there exist constants \(\gamma>1\) and \(\delta>0\) such that every always-correct Las Vegas word-RAM solution of the following three-phase problem has overhead \(\tau(n)=\Omega(n^\delta)\) for \(k=\lceil n^\gamma\rceil\)? Phase I preprocesses \(S_1,\ldots,S_k\subseteq[n]\) in expected \(O(kn\tau(n))\) time; Phase II receives \(T\subseteq[n]\) and takes expected \(O(n\tau(n))\) time; Phase III receives \(i\in[k]\) and decides whether \(S_i\cap T=\varnothing\) in expected \(O(\tau(n))\) time.
definitions: A uniform sequential word RAM has a fixed finite program, word-sized registers and addressed memory cells. Unit-cost instructions are reads and writes, comparisons, branching, addition, subtraction, multiplication, integer division with nonzero divisor, Boolean bit operations and logical shifts. Arithmetic stored in one word is modulo \(2^w\); shifts by at least \(w\) yield zero. Addresses must fit the available word size. All table construction and input-dependent auxiliary memory count; there is no free advice or input-dependent oracle. Randomized programs may generate independent uniform random words. A candidate program chooses a fixed integer \(a\ge2\) and uses words of \(w=\lceil a\log_2(n+k+2)\rceil\) bits. All its addresses must fit in one word, so the available address space is polynomial; the lower-bound claim quantifies over every such fixed \(a\). Sets may be given as incidence vectors, so their input lengths are \(kn\) and \(n\) bits. One uniform finite program for each phase must work for all \(n\) in the selected \(k=\lceil n^\gamma\rceil\) regime. The program may retain its computed memory between phases; all computation, initialization and copying are charged to the phase performing them. Phase I does not know \(T\) or \(i\), Phase II does not know \(i\), and Phase III receives only the index plus the retained state. Inputs are fixed independently of the random bits. Answers are always correct and each phase terminates almost surely; expected bounds hold for every fixed complete input. Define overhead as the maximum of 1 and the three worst-input expected phase costs divided respectively by \(kn,n,1\). A constant-factor asymptotic lower bound is required for all sufficiently large \(n\); a conditional hardness proof is not an unconditional resolution.
why: The multiphase conjecture is a central candidate for proving polynomial operation lower bounds for dynamic data structures.

context_blocks.text: Pătrașcu introduces this staged set-disjointness task and shows how its hardness would transfer to dynamic problems. The issue is a polynomial overhead, not merely a logarithmic lower bound.
Ko and Weinstein obtain strong lower bounds under a restriction on query adaptivity. Their result does not cover unrestricted adaptive queries.

answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked proof of the stated existence claim or its logical negation, with the same inputs, computation model, space allowance, quantifiers and cost guarantees. A result for a restricted input family or a different model does not decide the full target.
status_note: Open in the cited dated sources. The bounded source and subsequent-result review on 13 September 2026 found no verified resolution of this target; this is not exhaustive certification of current openness.

notes: Preserves the three charged phases of the original word-RAM problem and makes the zero-error expected-cost convention explicit. The distinct unrestricted-preprocessing cell-probe and semi-adaptive formulations are context, not asserted equivalent.
statement_review.scope: Formulation and bounded source review; no independent verification of new preprint proofs.

importance.reason: The multiphase conjecture is a central candidate for proving polynomial operation lower bounds for dynamic data structures.

category_assignment.reason: The staged data-structure interface and its charged preprocessing, update and query phases are the target.

sentences: The first phase stores a family of sets.
A later phase receives another set before the final query index is known.
The last phase asks whether that set intersects one chosen stored set.
The conjecture requires polynomial overhead in at least one normalized phase cost.
An unconditional proof would support strong dynamic-data-structure lower bounds.
